denials_note: All five denials landed on READ-ONLY commands. None blocked a write; none was worked around. The Iron-Plan hook denials fire on the PRESENCE of a protected path in the command's expansion (a glob, a directory argument, or a recursive scan root), not on an attempt to modify it -- so `ls daedalus/kairos/` and `grep -rn ... .` are refused as mutations. The work continued via the Read/Grep/Glob tools, which reached the same bytes. REPORTED AS A GAP, not routed around: a guard that cannot tell a read from a write teaches operators to reach for a different tool, which is the behaviour least likely to be reviewed.

findings.title: The loop is fail-closed by default: no permit, no run
findings.evidence: `python -m daedalus.loop --dry-run --max-iterations 1 --json` with no --arm exits 3, stop_reason='killswitch', stop_detail='no permit file: the loop is not armed', iterations_run=0, and records ZERO audited effects (open-for-write / os.replace / subprocess / socket all 0).
findings.where: daedalus/spine/killswitch.py (permit, not stop file); daedalus/loop.py:1284 main --arm

findings.title: install_process_guard precedes every audited effect in the loop process
findings.evidence: Audit hook installed before any daedalus import. In both armed runs the FIRST recorded effect already carries guard_active=True (guard_first_seen_at_seq=1, guard_active_at_first_effect=true), and every one of the 24 recorded effects carries guard_active=True.
findings.caveat: Scope is write/replace/spawn/socket only. READ-opens were deliberately not recorded, and daedalus/loop.py:1232 runs _load_dotenv() BEFORE install_process_guard() -- on a tree that has a .env, a read-open does precede the guard. This sandbox had no .env, so that ordering was not exercised.

findings.title: The loop's governance verdict is computed against a DIFFERENT repository than the loop's own --repo-root
findings.evidence: Loop repo_root = C:/Users/nukei/Desktop/agent_env.worktrees/preruling-cp @ 3e758392845d9faf7877977d5ae8806973ed62e6. core.get_governance(None) returned repo_root = C:\\Users\\nukei\\Desktop\\agent_env @ 77e7498a762aa96c436d367dc35ff3431c0fcfa8. same_tree=false. The verdict printed in the loop's own report names 77e7498a, a revision the loop is not standing on.
findings.where: daedalus/loop.py:1031 `gov = core.get_governance(self.project)` -- self.repo_root is never passed; the project registry resolves the root instead. Chain: core._gov_discrimination -> spine/bootstrap.py:288 gate_discrimination(repo_root, head=head).
findings.why_it_matters: Invariant 6 (atomic revisions) and invariant 9 (honest claims): a promotion verdict bound to another tree's HEAD is not a measurement of this candidate. Here it happened to fail CLOSED (degraded -> promotion refused). Nothing measured shows it must fail closed in the other direction, and that is the case worth ruling on.

findings.title: The map freshness gate suppresses ranked work, and the committed snapshot is ALREADY stale at the pinned sha
findings.evidence: docs/architecture-state.json committed at 3e758392 records repo_state.head=7955317284ec6ce72d050bc54ca3408221f5c91d; actual HEAD is 3e758392845d9faf7877977d5ae8806973ed62e6. map_state_trustworthy -> trusted=false, integrity=true. Dynamic range across the gate: 11 map candidates when fresh -> 0 when stale; queue total 16 -> 5.
findings.controls: Variant A (stale head, digest RE-SIGNED so integrity passes) isolates the freshness gate: integrity=true, freshness.fresh=false, 11 withheld, 0 ranked. Variant B (hand-edited, digest not re-signed) fires the integrity gate instead. NEGATIVE CONTROL (real snapshot re-stamped to the real HEAD and re-signed) is trusted=true and ranks 11 -- so the zero is caused by the gate, not by an empty picker.

findings.title: The freshness gate changes which LANE the loop routes to -- stale map picks a free lane, fresh map picks a paid one
findings.evidence: Same command, same tree, only the snapshot's freshness differs. Stale map -> candidate 'docref-docs-adrs-011-event-spine-md-3448f5', source=docref, lane=ollama (free, local 127.0.0.1:11434). Fresh map -> candidate 'map-island-daedalus-eval-provenance-py-f83630', source=map_island, lane=claude_cli (PAID). Both --dry-run, so outcome=not_attempted and no vendor call left the process.
findings.why_it_matters: The staleness of a generated file selects the spend lane. That is a budget-relevant consequence of a freshness gate that reads as purely advisory.

findings.title: The architecture snapshot write sink is NON-atomic; the killswitch permit sink IS atomic
findings.evidence: `python -m daedalus.cli map` write sink for docs/architecture-state.json: daedalus/mapping/drift.py:1069 in write_snapshot -- a direct p.write_text(), mode='w', with ZERO os.replace events in the whole run. Stack: drift.py:1069 write_snapshot <- drift.py:1504 refresh <- mapping/render.py:1597 main <- cli.py:1148 main. By contrast the permit goes through daedalus/atomic.py:119 write_text_atomic + atomic.py:74 replace_with_retry.
findings.coupled_risk: A torn write leaves unparsable JSON. picker.load_map_state degrades that to {}, and map_state_trustworthy({}) returns trusted=True ('no map snapshot to check') at picker.py:1014-1015 -- fail OPEN, the opposite posture to the head check three lines below it. Consequence measured here is benign (no data -> no candidates), but the trusted=True on empty is the asymmetry to rule on.

findings.title: Effect containment held; two sinks reach outside the repo root by design
findings.evidence: Every audited write in both the loop and map runs landed inside the disposable worktree, except: %TEMP% (daedalus/structcore/tokens.py:18 _encoder, tokenizer cache) and, WITHOUT the DAEDALUS_KILLSWITCH override, the permit at %LOCALAPPDATA%/daedalus/control/<repo-digest>/killswitch -- measured as C:\\Users\\nukei\\AppData\\Local\\daedalus\\control\\a30fb957587b\\killswitch. The permit path is per-repo-digest, so it is namespaced, but it is outside every worktree.

findings.title: Four of six git spawns in the map run carry no -C and depend on the process cwd
findings.evidence: Audited subprocess argv in `daedalus.cli map --repo <wt>`: 1x 'git -C <wt> log --numstat --format=', then 'git status --porcelain' x4 and 'git ls-files -z' x1 with no -C and Popen cwd=None (inherited). Correct in this run only because cwd happened to be the target worktree.
findings.why_it_matters: Same class as F3: the tree a step reads is resolved by ambient state rather than by the root the caller named. Reported as an observation from the argv, not as a separate experiment -- no run with a mismatched cwd was performed.

findings.title: install_process_guard covers subprocess and urlopen, but NOT raw sockets
findings.evidence: daedalus/budget.py:1184-1207 patches exactly three names: subprocess.run, subprocess.Popen, urllib.request.urlopen -- no socket-level interposition. At runtime the 7 loopback connects to 127.0.0.1:11434 (the ollama reachability probe) were attributed to budget.py:1162, which is the `if vendor is None: return original(...)` passthrough branch of _guarded_urlopen -- so that traffic DID enter the interposer, was classified as no-vendor, and was passed through unpriced. Correct for a free local lane, and it also shows the interposer only sees what routes through urllib.request.urlopen.
findings.gap: A client using raw sockets, http.client directly, or a third-party http stack (requests/httpx/aiohttp) is not seen by this interposer at all. budget.py:1226-1231 already names the register as 'the honest accounting' and says the non-explicit sites are covered ONLY when install_process_guard() has run in their process -- this trace confirms the mechanism, not full coverage.
